Definition: from G3326 and G906; to throw over, i.e. (middle voice figuratively) to turn about in opinion:--change mind.
BiblicalUsage: The islanders watching Paul after the snakebite changed their minds about him, first expecting him to swell up and die, then deciding he must be a god. The word is the turning of an opinion, and Luke uses it for a crowd that got the man completely wrong in both directions.
TheologicalSignificance: I take this as a warning about crowds: the same people who were sure Paul would drop dead were just as sure, minutes later, that he was a god, and both judgments were hasty.
